summary: Product launches, model releases, security incidents, platform changes, outages, and earnings-driven product news. The story is the product / model / incident itself, not the share-price reaction.
fits_when: primary_entities includes a software vendor, hardware vendor, model publisher, platform operator, or security researcher
the news is a product / model / incident; market reaction is secondary
fits_poorly_when: the load-bearing claim is the share-price move (use finance)
the news is a regulator's rule about tech (use policy)
the news is a state-level export ban or sanctions on tech (use geopolitics)

vendor_independence_rules.vendor_benchmarks_are_not_independent: spec figures from a vendor's own launch page must be attributed to the vendor, never rendered as third-party fact
vendor_independence_rules.ga_vs_beta_vs_preview: always name the release stage; 'GA', 'beta', 'developer preview', 'limited rollout' are different stories
vendor_independence_rules.scope_claims_for_outages: outage scope figures (% of internet, % of users) require a measurement source — Cloudflare Radar, Downdetector aggregates, the platform's own status page
vendor_independence_rules.model_capability_claims: benchmark numbers must cite the benchmark name AND who ran it (vendor, third-party lab, paper)

preferred_pattern.describes: named developer / customer audience with a count
the spec or capability change with attribution
the comparison vs prior version, peer model, or industry baseline
rollout window, deprecation date, or next milestone

notes: Data modules are common — most tech stories have a benchmark, context window, throughput figure, or pricing point.
Quote modules from a vendor's launch keynote are valuable when transcribed verbatim in 02_evidence.quotes.
Map modules are rare; only useful for geographic outage maps or rollout-region stories.

asset_hint_policy.data: the workhorse for tech — benchmarks, context windows, throughput, pricing all become data modules
asset_hint_policy.mute: use when the spoken claim is the asset (e.g., a strategic decision, a deprecation announcement)
asset_hint_policy.photo: permitted when 02_evidence references an official product image from the vendor's press kit; never stock 'person using laptop' imagery
asset_hint_policy.map: only for geographic outage maps or regional rollout charts; rare

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Stock 'person typing on laptop' / 'glowing AI brain' / 'data streams' imagery
banned_visual_patterns.why: Generic; reduces credibility; visual-safety identity-implication risk for AI-face stocks
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Data module with the actual benchmark or spec

banned_visual_patterns.why: Reads as advertising; primary asset should be the spec or the chart
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Logo permitted as L3 chip; data is the primary asset

banned_visual_patterns.why: Filler; reduces seriousness; dates the video stylistically

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Cropped CEO headshot for keynote announcement
banned_visual_patterns.why: Personality-coverage when the story is the product
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Photo only when 02_evidence explicitly references a press-kit keynote photo with the CEO as the named subject; otherwise data or mute

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Generic 'AI face' imagery for an AI / model story
banned_visual_patterns.why: Identity-implication blocker; suggests anthropomorphism that the evidence doesn't support
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Data module with benchmarks or context window numbers

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Marketing-hero shot of a phone/laptop with the launch keynote backdrop
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Permitted if attributed via L3 chip ('Apple keynote · Sept 9'); otherwise data or mute

lead_with: the vendor's own announcement / model card / launch page (attributed)
the post-mortem or status page for outages
the security advisory / CVE record for vulnerabilities
the third-party benchmark paper / lab report
second_tier: Verge / Ars Technica / Bloomberg reporting that quotes the vendor
GitHub release notes for open-source projects
App-store or Play-store listings for app changes
treat_with_caution: vendor benchmarks — quote, but always attribute ('per Apple's M5 launch page')
anonymous engineers / 'people familiar with' on roadmap leaks
tweets unless from official vendor accounts
must_cite_explicitly: every spec — context window size, parameter count, throughput, price-per-token
every release stage (GA, beta, preview, internal)

patterns.name: ship-with-delta
patterns.example: OpenAI shipped GPT-5 on Wednesday, raising the API context limit from 128k to 1M tokens.

patterns.name: outage-scope
patterns.shape: <vendor>'s <service> took <scope> offline at <UTC time>; the company restored service in <window>.
patterns.example: Cloudflare's edge briefly took 23% of the public internet offline at 14:17 UTC; the company restored service in 38 minutes.

patterns.name: platform-policy-change
patterns.shape: <vendor> removed <feature> from <product line> on <day>, ending a <duration> run.
patterns.example: Apple removed the Lightning port from the entire iPad lineup on Tuesday, ending a 13-year run.

patterns.name: security-incident
patterns.shape: <vendor> disclosed a <CVE class> in <product>; <scope> exposed before <patch-window>.
patterns.example: Microsoft disclosed an authentication-bypass flaw in Exchange Server; CVE-2025-12345, exposed for 11 days before the patch.

patterns.name: model-benchmark
patterns.example: Anthropic's Claude 4.7 scored 78.3% on SWE-bench Verified, up 12.4 points from 4.6.

first_4_words_must_contain: the vendor proper name (Apple, Microsoft, OpenAI, Cloudflare, Anthropic)
OR a model / product proper name (GPT-5, Claude 4.7, Llama 4)
banned_constructions: questions ('Will this AI model change everything?')
'Big news for tech today...' generic openers

good: OpenAI shipped GPT-5 on Wednesday, raising the API context limit from 128k to 1M tokens.
Cloudflare's edge briefly took 23% of the public internet offline at 14:17 UTC.
Apple removed the Lightning port from the entire iPad lineup on Tuesday.
bad: Could this be the AI model that changes everything?
Big news for the tech world today.
OpenAI just released a revolutionary new model.

subtitle_guidance.L1_role: the spec delta or incident scope
L2_rules: always include release stage (GA, beta, preview)
always include the time of an incident or rollout date
L3_rules: name the source — vendor page, status page, benchmark, advisory
for vendor-published claims, L3 must say so ('per Apple', 'OpenAI claims')
type_specific_rules: Model names use vendor capitalisation (GPT-5, Claude 4.7, Gemini 2.5).
Benchmark names use the benchmark's canonical capitalisation (SWE-bench, MMLU, HellaSwag).
Spec deltas use → not 'to' in subtitles ('128K → 1M' not '128K to 1M').
CVE ids appear in L3 in canonical form (CVE-2025-12345).

module_selection_hints.include_data_when: ANY benchmark, spec, throughput, price, context window, or scope figure — most tech stories
module_selection_hints.include_quote_when: 02_evidence.quotes has a verbatim line from the vendor's launch keynote, blog post, or security advisory
module_selection_hints.include_map_when: outage has a regional dimension OR rollout is staged geographically; otherwise skip
module_selection_hints.stakes_module_must_name: the developer / customer audience with a count ('the 4 million developers on the API', '1.2 billion iPad owners', '23% of internet routes')

anti_patterns.pattern: Vendor benchmark rendered as third-party fact
anti_patterns.shape: Hook says 'the fastest model ever' citing only the vendor's launch page
anti_patterns.why: Vendor benchmarks aren't independent; this is brand copy in a news frame
anti_patterns.fix: Attribute: 'per OpenAI's launch page' / 'Anthropic claims' / 'Apple's own benchmarks'

anti_patterns.shape: Hook or stakes uses one of these adjectives
anti_patterns.why: Banned by playbook §1.4 and tech-type rules
anti_patterns.fix: State the spec delta numerically: '128K → 1M context', '+12.4 pts vs prior'

anti_patterns.shape: 'OpenAI launched GPT-5 today' when only a research preview is available
anti_patterns.fix: Always name the release stage in the script and L2 ('research preview · API only · waitlist')

anti_patterns.pattern: Outage scope claim with no measurement source
anti_patterns.shape: 'Took half the internet down' with no Cloudflare Radar / Downdetector / status-page citation
anti_patterns.why: Single-source / unsourced scope is a sourcing failure
anti_patterns.fix: Cite the measurement: 'per Cloudflare Radar', 'per Downdetector aggregate spike'

anti_patterns.pattern: 'Person using laptop' stock imagery for tech stories
anti_patterns.why: Says nothing about the specific story; identity-implication risk
anti_patterns.fix: Data module with the spec / benchmark

anti_patterns.shape: Stakes says 'the model thinks / believes / wants'
anti_patterns.fix: State capability: 'the model now handles 1M tokens', 'the model scored 78.3% on SWE-bench'

anti_patterns.shape: 'And this is just the beginning of the AI revolution'
anti_patterns.fix: Close anchors on a concrete date: 'public rollout begins November 14', 'deprecation deadline March 31', 'next benchmark drop December 5'

anti_patterns.pattern: Citing a tweet as primary source
anti_patterns.shape: Evidence module attributes to '@vendor on X'
anti_patterns.why: Tweets are not primary unless they are the official disclosure (rare for outages)
anti_patterns.fix: Cite the official launch post, status-page entry, or model card; tweets are L3-tier sourcing only when they ARE the disclosure

stage_2_extra_checks: verify every benchmark number names the benchmark (which one) AND who ran it (vendor / third-party)
verify every release-stage claim has a source (vendor page, status page, advisory)
verify outage-scope claims trace to a measurement source, not just wire reporting
stage_5_extra_checks: scan 03_script.md for banned moralisers: revolutionary, game-changing, next-gen, mind-blowing, paradigm-shift
verify every benchmark figure has both the benchmark name and 'per <vendor / lab>' attribution in the script
verify release stage is named in script (GA, beta, preview, limited rollout) — not just 'launched'
verify close anchors on a concrete date or milestone
